test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 27 Sept 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: What is non-tax revenue?

options.text: Income earned by the government through the public sector units only
Financial help in the form of grants, gifts from foreign governments and international organisations
Recurring income earned by the government from sources other than taxes

solution:
The correct answer is __**Recurring income earned by the government from sources other than taxes**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Non-tax revenue refers to the **Recurring income earned by the government from sources other than taxes** .
 
• **This includes:**
 
 
• Fees and fines collected by the government.
 
• Profits from public sector enterprises.
 
• Dividends and interest received from investments.
 
• Charges for services like water supply, electricity, and railways.
 
• Income from government-owned assets, such as rent and royalties on natural resources.
 
• Grants and donations from foreign governments and international organizations.
 
 
 
• It is a part of revenue receipts, which are the inflows of funds to the government from all sources.
 
• The approximations of non-tax revenue receipts from a range of sources, including interest, fees, fines, and other miscellaneous receipts collected during the exercise of sovereign functions, regulatory and license fees, and user fees for goods and services made available to the public.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Revenue receipt refers to the income received by the government in the normal course of its business activities, such as taxes, duties, fees, and other charges.
 
• GST (Goods and Services Tax) is a tax levied on the supply of goods and services in India.
 
• It is a revenue receipt for the government, as it is collected on behalf of the government by the businesses that are registered under GST.
 
• Receipts from sale of shares of public sector companies is a capital receipt as it involves the sale of assets.
 
• Recovery of loans is also a capital receipt as it involves the recovery of loans given by the government.
 
• Borrowings from public is a capital receipt as it involves the borrowing of funds by the government from the public.
 
• Capital receipts are those that either increase the government's liabilities or lower the value of its assets.
 
 
• In essence, these are the loans that the government has obtained from a variety of sources to pay for long-term developmental requirements.
 
• They are non-recurring in nature.
